title: Grandfather's curfew and the uncle who was whipped and thrown out
summary: A young uncle sneaks in past curfew, is whipped, leaves the house and never returns; Cobb stresses his grandfather's stern convictions.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: You were saying earlier, though, that your father ran a very strict house with the TIME
My grandfather.
Your grandfather with the time when the kids had to be in at night.
So I had a young uncle -- see, his curfew -- he had curfew hours for ones of certain ages for
12:00 o'clock that was of that age, and the ones that were older, 1:00 o'clock. So that made an hour differential in the two different age groups.

So one night my young uncle had the 1:00 o'clock curfew and once that it happened, he'd slip that key and that's it, you're locked out. And the girls let him through a window. He knew what the policy was so he didn't -- it's not like he'd come and knock on the door and get in. He didn't want Papa to know nothing about nothing. He (unintelligible) and them girls let him in, but he knew he was in there.
WENT TO THE WINDOW AND KNOCKED ON THE WINDOW

The next day he come home from his work. He had platted some leather and made a good whip out of it. And knotted it on the end in three plats. And when he walked in the door he just started to lash it. Pow Pow Pow. He said, "Papa, what you doing?" He said, "I told you if you live under my roof, you'll abide by my law." He said, "Well, Papa, I'm grown up." "If you're that grown, get your THINGS packed up and get out." So he did. He packed up and got out and never come back anymore. That was a stern, firm father. You know, what they say today, that's the wrong way to go.
Well, did he never come back at all?
Not even to --
No, sir.
-- talk --
I said, no, sir. He made his own life until
death. He died in '45 and I was in Washington, D. C. at the Howard Theater when my mother called me and told me he passed.
Well, I mean, did any of you kids who knew him (unintelligible) ever see him?
We saw him, sure.
Oh, you did. Yeah, I see. You just didn't --
But his father didn't see him.
Oh, I've got you.

And his father didn't look for him after he told him to get out. He didn't for his father after he told him to get out. That's how firm the situation was. But he was -- my grandfather was a man that stood on his own convictions, meant every word he said. And that's the way it was.
